```{r setup}
#| include: false
lib <- Sys.glob("../renv/library/*/R-4.6/*")
.libPaths(c(lib, .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(knitr) })

data_dir <- Sys.getenv("TESI_DATA")
stopifnot("TESI_DATA not set" = nzchar(data_dir), dir.exists(data_dir))
pilot_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "derived", "pilot")
ref_dir   <- file.path(data_dir, "derived", "reference")
pcal_dir  <- file.path(data_dir, "derived", "p_calibration")
tissues <- c("colon", "lymphoid", "brain")

# read <tissue>_<variant>_pilot_<what>.csv (variant "crule", "crule_hd" or "crule_hd_s100"); NULL (with a note) if missing
rd_pilot <- function(tissue, what, variant = "crule") {
  f <- file.path(pilot_dir, sprintf("%s_%s_pilot_%s.csv", tissue, variant, what))
  if (!file.exists(f)) { message("missing: ", f); return(NULL) }
  read.csv(f, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
# pilot at the HD level of the main run: colon = c-rule rows at 175 UMI per cell (HD level 174),
# lymph node and brain = HD pilots with RCTD UMI_min_sigma = 100 (DECISIONS 2026-11-12, 2026-11-17)
rd_hd <- function(tissue, what) {
  if (tissue != "colon") return(rd_pilot(tissue, what, variant = "crule_hd_s100"))
  x <- rd_pilot(tissue, what)
  if (!is.null(x) && "depth" %in% names(x)) x <- x[x$depth == 175, ]
  x
}
show_pilot <- function(what, n = 20) {
  for (t in tissues) {
    x <- rd_pilot(t, what)
    cat("\n\n**", t, "**\n\n", sep = "")
    if (is.null(x)) cat("*not available yet*\n") else print(kable(head(x, n)))
  }
}
# run a test script from thesis/ and keep its PASS/FAIL lines
run_test <- function(f) {
  owd <- setwd(".."); on.exit(setwd(owd))
  out <- capture.output(try(source(f, local = new.env()), silent = TRUE))
  grep("PASS|FAIL", out, value = TRUE)
}
```

**Single goal.** Fix the study protocol (ADEMP) before any result, and run a declared pilot whose only use is to give the values the pre-registered rules need. These are the SD of the paired differences for n_sim, runtimes, failures, seed check and depth reached (ADEMP §10). Pilot numbers do not enter the thesis results.

**Dependencies.** T1 (datasets, split). **Branch.** `thesis/expression-sources`. **Data.** `TESI_DATA` on lesexp (`/mnt/micron/geo_spatialtrans/tesi_pp1209/data`).

**Status of the pilot inputs.** Pilot references were rebuilt with φ estimated on 50,000 cells after the failed φ check (DECISIONS 2026-11-11): colon and lymph node on 2026-11-12, brain on 2026-11-14. The colon pilot was rerun with the new φ on 2026-11-12 (the basis of n_sim = 118, DECISIONS 2026-11-12). The lymph node and brain pilots were rerun with the new φ on 2026-11-17, at the HD level of each tissue only (62 and 121 UMI per cell; `<tissue>_crule_hd_pilot_*`), as Luca asked on 2026-11-16 (same row), and again with RCTD `UMI_min_sigma` = 100 after RCTD stopped on every 2-cell dataset (`<tissue>_crule_hd_s100_pilot_*`, DECISIONS 2026-11-17). Sections 3.1, 4.1, 4.2 and 5.2 show the c-rule pilots of 9–11/11 first and then the HD level of the main run (colon c-rule rows at 175 UMI per cell, lymph node and brain HD pilots with `UMI_min_sigma` = 100); n_sim (§5.1) uses the HD level only.

# 1. Pre-registration

Written before the pilot runs. Full text in `protocol/ADEMP.md` (v1.5, 2026-11-12); approved by Luca on 2026-11-18 (DECISIONS 2026-11-18).

| Item | Rule fixed before the pilot | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Pilot scope | three tissues, arms E and C− plus the real anchor, CPU methods (RCTD, spatialDWLS, MuSiC, NNLS), 10 replicates per arm × condition; pilot held-out and E′ donors sampled from training (seed 20261030) | ADEMP §10; DECISIONS 2026-10-30 |
| n_sim | 2 × MCSE of the paired RMSE difference ≤ δ/2, SD = upper 95% limit from the pilot, δ = 0.02 | DECISIONS 2026-11-03 (two rows) |
| Dirichlet concentration | α_k = c · p_k, c = median over R6 ROIs per tissue and cells level | DECISIONS 2026-11-06 |
| Depth thinning | exact downsampling to the target, report spots below target | DECISIONS 2026-11-02 |
| Estimand | cell share for every method (main); UMI share as sensitivity | DECISIONS 2026-11-03 |
| Failures | null-baseline fill, no exclusion threshold, common-spot set as sensitivity, tolerance 1e-4 (1e-5 until 2026-11-17; failures at 1e-5 as sensitivity) | DECISIONS 2026-11-02, 2026-11-03 (two rows); ADEMP §7.2, §12 (2026-11-17) |
| Null baseline | observed RMSE within 0.005 of the Dirichlet-multinomial formula | ADEMP §7.2 item 3; `scripts/06b_pilot_nsim.R` (2026-11-05) |
| φ sample | r(log φ) ≥ 0.99 and median ratio 0.95–1.05, else 50,000 cells | DECISIONS 2026-10-29 |
| Reference cap | 1,000 cells per type kept if r ≥ 0.99 per type | DECISIONS 2026-11-04 |
| P marker cap | Jaccard ≥ 0.9 per type in the lymph node at 10,000 cells, else 20,000 | DECISIONS 2026-11-11 |

## Deviations from the pre-registration (recorded, not corrected)

- The φ sample check was run on 2026-11-11, after the pilots, although it was due before them (DECISIONS 2026-11-11).
- The pilots ran at 175 and 4,900 UMI per cell in every tissue. After the pilots the design kept one Visium HD level per tissue, 174 (colon), 62 (lymph node) and 121 (brain) UMI per cell (DECISIONS 2026-11-12, PROTOCOLLO 1.5). For the colon n_sim uses only the 175 rows, whose depth matches the colon HD level (174).
- Lymph node and brain pilots first used φ from 20,000 cells. As Luca asked on 2026-11-16, they were rerun on 2026-11-17 with φ from 50,000 cells at the HD level of each tissue, and these reruns give their n_sim (DECISIONS 2026-11-12, precised 2026-11-16).
- The first colon pilot was rerun after two fixes: MuSiC failed on every spot for a code error, which also emptied the common-spot set (DECISIONS 2026-11-02, failures), and binomial thinning was replaced by exact thinning because the depth check assumed an exact target (DECISIONS 2026-11-02, thinning).
- The Dirichlet concentration changed while the colon pilot was running (c = K · p_k, then c = 1, then the R6 rule of DECISIONS 2026-11-06). The values passed to the protocol come from the c-rule pilots only (`<tissue>_crule_pilot_*`); the earlier runs are kept in `derived/pilot/colon_c1`, `colon_c9` (ADEMP §6).
- The pre-registered residue check (C10) failed in the lymph node c-rule pilot: RCTD returned 4 negative values in arm C−, the smallest −1.37e-5, below the tolerance −1e-5, so under the pre-registered rule those values would have counted as failed spots. As pre-registered, the tolerance was revised before any result, by the rule "smallest power of ten above the largest residue over all pilots" (HD pilots included), to 1e-4; failure rates at 1e-5 are kept as a sensitivity (ADEMP §7.2, §12, 2026-11-17).
- spatialDWLS spot clustering moved from k-means (no source) to Leiden with the Spotless parameters (DECISIONS 2026-11-04). n_sim rose from 81 to 217 in the colon after this change; the rule was kept, because changing it once we knew which pairs raise n_sim would be a post-hoc adjustment (DECISIONS 2026-11-03, precision of 2026-11-06).

The two tests that run in seconds are rerun at every render.

```{r check-c}
for (f in c("tests/test_split.R", "tests/test_simulate.R")) {
  r <- run_test(f)
  cat("\n", f, ": ", sum(grepl("PASS", r)), " PASS, ", sum(grepl("FAIL", r)), " FAIL\n", sep = "")
  cat(paste0("  ", r), sep = "\n")
}
```

**C10, numerical residues.** Raw estimates of the c-rule pilots, before `clean_props()` (`scripts/06d_pilot_residues.R <tissue> rule`). The script reproduces the colon values of ADEMP §7.2 on the first colon pilot (RCTD 2 negative values of 1,079,892, smallest −6.98e-7; largest |sum − 1| 8.9e-16; run of 2026-11-16).

```{r residues}
#| results: asis
for (t in tissues) {
  x <- rd_pilot(t, "residues")
  cat("\n\n**", t, "**\n\n", sep = "")
  if (is.null(x)) { cat("*not available yet*\n"); next }
  for (v in c("min_value", "max_dev_ok")) x[[v]] <- formatC(x[[v]], format = "e", digits = 2)
  print(kable(x[, c("method", "dataset", "values", "n_neg", "min_value", "n_grey_neg", "n_fail_neg",
                    "max_dev_ok", "n_grey_sum", "n_fail_sum", "pass_1e5", "pass")], row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\nPre-registered check at 1e-5:", if (all(x$pass_1e5)) "PASS" else "FAIL", "\n")
  cat("\nCheck at the amended tolerance 1e-4 (ADEMP §12, 2026-11-17):", if (all(x$pass)) "PASS" else "FAIL", "\n")
}
```

# 3. Check B — biological plausibility

## 3.1 Depth reached by arms and anchor

Share of spots at and below the target, per arm, anchor and condition (DECISIONS 2026-11-02).

```{r depth}
#| results: asis
for (t in tissues) {
  x <- rd_pilot(t, "depth")
  cat("\n\n**", t, "**\n\n", sep = "")
  if (is.null(x)) { cat("*not available yet*\n"); next }
  a <- aggregate(cbind(n_at_target, n_below) ~ n_cells + depth + dataset, x, sum)
  a$pct_below <- round(100 * a$n_below / (a$n_at_target + a$n_below), 1)
  print(kable(a))
}
```

At 175 UMI per cell every spot of every arm and of the anchor reached its target in the three tissues, so the depth is the same everywhere and differences between arms come from μ. At 4,900 UMI per cell part of the spots stayed below target, and differently in the anchor and the arms (lymph node, 10 cells: 33% of anchor spots against 53% in E; brain, 2 cells: 41% against 18%). There the difference from the anchor mixed the source of μ with depth, which is why the level was removed (DECISIONS 2026-11-12). The table below shows the HD level of the main run (62–174 UMI per cell), with the number of spots below target in the line under it.

```{r depth-hd}
#| results: asis
dh <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) {
  x <- rd_hd(t, "depth")
  if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)
  cbind(tissue = t, aggregate(cbind(n_at_target, n_below) ~ n_cells + depth + dataset, x, sum))
}))
if (is.null(dh)) cat("*not available yet*\n") else {
  print(kable(dh, row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\n\nSpots below target at the HD level:", sum(dh$n_below), "of", sum(dh$n_at_target + dh$n_below), "\n")
}
```

## 3.2 Library sizes by cell type

Median library size of the training cells of each spot type (pilot references, `L_by_type`).

```{r libsize}
#| results: asis
for (t in tissues) {
  f <- file.path(ref_dir, paste0(t, "_pilot.rds"))
  cat("\n\n**", t, "**\n\n", sep = "")
  if (!file.exists(f)) { cat("*not available yet*\n"); next }
  R0 <- readRDS(f)
  L <- R0$L_by_type[R0$types_spot]
  tab <- data.frame(type = names(L), cells = lengths(L),
                    median_umi = vapply(L, median, numeric(1)),
                    q25 = vapply(L, quantile, numeric(1), 0.25),
                    q75 = vapply(L, quantile, numeric(1), 0.75))
  print(kable(tab[order(-tab$median_umi), ], row.names = FALSE, digits = 0))
  rm(R0); invisible(gc())
}
```

In the colon, epithelial tumour cells carry several times the RNA of lymphocytes (first pilot reference: EpiT median 12,453 UMI against 2,146–2,298 for TCD8 and TCD4; DECISIONS 2026-11-03). This is expected biology (large, transcriptionally active epithelial cells against small resting T cells) and it explains why RCTD, which estimates the share of UMI, overestimates EpiT when read as a share of cells. The gap depends only on the library sizes, which are the same in every arm, so it does not bias the comparison between sources of μ (DECISIONS 2026-11-03, estimand).

## 3.3 Cell-type diagnostics

Per replicate: bias per spot type and proportion assigned to types absent from the spots (false positives).

```{r types}
#| results: asis
show_pilot("type_diagnostics")
```

## 3.4 Arm P calibration

Markers per type of the P calibration (`scripts/04p_calibrate_p.R`; `findMarkers` on at most 20,000 training cells per type, DECISIONS 2026-11-11; FDR 0.05, and 0.01 as the pre-registered check).

```{r pcal}
#| results: asis
for (t in tissues) {
  f <- file.path(pcal_dir, paste0(t, "_p_calibration.rds"))
  cat("\n\n**", t, "**\n\n", sep = "")
  if (!file.exists(f)) { cat("*not available yet*\n"); next }
  pc <- readRDS(f)
  cat("marker cap:", pc$settings$marker_cap, "cells per type; cells used for markers:",
      format(pc$n_marker_cells, big.mark = ","), "of", format(pc$n_cells, big.mark = ","), "\n\n")
  if (pc$settings$marker_cap != 20000) cat("**WARNING: cap differs from 20,000 (DECISIONS 2026-11-11)**\n\n")
  print(kable(pc$n_markers, row.names = FALSE))
}
```

With `pval.type = "some"` every type has markers, so no two P types share a profile (with `"all"` 7 of 18 colon types had none; DECISIONS 2026-11-04). Raising the cap from 10,000 to 20,000 changed the number of markers per type by at most 8 (pdc 49 against 41; DECISIONS 2026-11-11). Note carried to T3: in the brain the upper tail of the gene means differs between P and the real data (brain calibration 2026-11-11, ADEMP §2.1): the 99th percentile is lower in P (0.78 against 1.93) and the 99.9th is higher (10.7 against 5.8), so P has fewer moderately high genes and a few more extreme ones. This is to be checked in the Aim 1 distribution measures (ADEMP §5.1).

# 4. Counter-proof

## 4.1 C− against E

If C− gave the same errors as E, the benchmark would be insensitive to μ (ADEMP §9). Mean RMSE (cell-share truth, failed spots filled with the null baseline) at 175 UMI per cell.

```{r rmse}
#| results: asis
cm <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) {
  x <- rd_pilot(t, "rmse_methods")
  if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)
  x <- x[x$depth == 175 & x$dataset %in% c("E", "Cminus", "anchor"), ]
  w <- reshape(x[, c("n_cells", "method", "dataset", "mean_rmse")], idvar = c("n_cells", "method"),
               timevar = "dataset", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub("mean_rmse.", "", names(w))
  w$Cminus_minus_E <- w$Cminus - w$E
  cbind(tissue = t, w)
}))
if (is.null(cm)) cat("*not available yet*\n") else {
  print(kable(cm, row.names = FALSE, digits = 3))
  m <- cm[cm$method != "null baseline", ]
  cat("\n\nC− has a higher RMSE than E in", sum(m$Cminus_minus_E > 0), "of", nrow(m),
      "method × tissue × cells cells; the smallest gap is", round(min(m$Cminus_minus_E), 3), ".\n")
}
```

Failures point the same way. The table gives the failed spots of RCTD and spatialDWLS, summed over replicates, in the c-rule pilots at 175 UMI per cell and at the HD level of the main run (ADEMP §7.2; DECISIONS 2026-11-17).

```{r fails}
#| results: asis
fail_wide <- function(x, tissue, pilot) {
  if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0) return(NULL)
  x <- x[x$method %in% c("RCTD", "spatialDWLS") & x$dataset %in% c("E", "Cminus", "anchor"), ]
  w <- reshape(aggregate(fail_spots ~ n_cells + method + dataset, x, sum), idvar = c("n_cells", "method"),
               timevar = "dataset", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub("fail_spots.", "", names(w))
  cbind(tissue = tissue, pilot = pilot, w)
}
fl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) {
  a <- rd_pilot(t, "summary"); if (!is.null(a)) a <- a[a$depth == 175, ]
  rbind(fail_wide(a, t, "c-rule 175"), fail_wide(rd_hd(t, "summary"), t, "HD"))
}))
if (is.null(fl)) cat("*not available yet*\n") else print(kable(fl, row.names = FALSE))
```

**HD level of the main run.** The lymph node and brain pilots were rerun at their HD level (62 and 121 UMI per cell) with RCTD `UMI_min_sigma` = 100 (DECISIONS 2026-11-17). The colon HD level (174 UMI per cell) corresponds to the 175 rows of the table above.

```{r rmse-hd}
#| results: asis
mh <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("lymphoid", "brain"), function(t) {
  x <- rd_pilot(t, "rmse_methods", variant = "crule_hd_s100")
  if (is.null(x)) return(NULL)
  x <- x[x$dataset %in% c("E", "Cminus", "anchor"), ]
  w <- reshape(x[, c("n_cells", "method", "dataset", "mean_rmse")], idvar = c("n_cells", "method"),
               timevar = "dataset", direction = "wide")
  names(w) <- sub("mean_rmse.", "", names(w))
  w$Cminus_minus_E <- w$Cminus - w$E
  cbind(tissue = t, w)
}))
if (is.null(mh)) cat("*not available yet*\n") else {
  print(kable(mh, row.names = FALSE, digits = 4))
  m <- mh[mh$method != "null baseline", ]
  cat("\n\nC− has a higher RMSE than E in", sum(m$Cminus_minus_E > 0), "of", nrow(m),
      "method × tissue × cells cells; gaps below δ = 0.02:", sum(m$Cminus_minus_E < 0.02),
      "; the smallest gap is", round(min(m$Cminus_minus_E), 4), ".\n")
}
```

**Verdict.** PASS with a reservation. C− has a higher RMSE than E for every method, tissue and cells level, both at 175 UMI per cell (24 of 24) and at the HD levels of lymph node and brain (16 of 16). At 175 UMI per cell the smallest gap, 0.023, is larger than δ = 0.02, the smallest difference between methods that we consider relevant. At the HD levels two gaps are smaller than δ, both in the lymph node at 2 cells. They are MuSiC with 0.0047 (E 0.192, C− 0.197) and spatialDWLS with 0.017 (E 0.206, C− 0.223), and the other 14 are at least 0.029. In that condition both methods already have a higher RMSE than the null baseline (0.137) with the true μ, at about 124 UMI per spot (2 cells × 62 UMI per cell). They carry little information on the composition there, so permuting the genes cannot make them much worse. This is not a pre-registered failure, because ADEMP §9 judges C− on the main run (low fidelity and rankings different from the anchor). It is reported as a result and carried to T5, where the main run will show whether the gap stays below δ. NNLS and MuSiC are read next to the null baseline (4.2), which is close to an oracle in this design.

## 4.2 Null baseline

The null baseline gives every spot the training shares. Because α_k = c · p_k, the expected composition of every spot is p, so the null baseline is close to an oracle and its RMSE is fixed by the spread of the true compositions (ADEMP §7.2). Pre-registered check: observed null RMSE within 0.005 of the Dirichlet-multinomial formula.

```{r null}
#| results: asis
# formula values at 2 and 10 cells with the c rule (ADEMP §7.2 item 3; c does not depend on depth)
fml <- data.frame(tissue = rep(tissues, each = 2), n_cells = rep(c(2, 10), 3),
                  formula = c(0.182, 0.149, 0.137, 0.105, 0.134, 0.066))
nb <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) {
  a <- rd_pilot(t, "rmse_methods"); if (!is.null(a)) a <- a[a$depth == 175, ]
  b <- rd_hd(t, "rmse_methods")
  do.call(rbind, lapply(list(list(a, "c-rule 175"), list(b, "HD")), function(p) {
    x <- p[[1]]
    if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0) return(NULL)
    x <- x[x$method == "null baseline", c("n_cells", "dataset", "mean_rmse")]
    cbind(tissue = t, pilot = p[[2]], x)
  }))
}))
if (is.null(nb)) cat("*not available yet*\n") else {
  nb <- merge(nb, fml)
  nb$obs_minus_formula <- nb$mean_rmse - nb$formula
  print(kable(nb, row.names = FALSE, digits = 4))
  cat("\n\nLargest |observed − formula|:", round(max(abs(nb$obs_minus_formula)), 4),
      "(formula rounded to 3 decimals); pre-registered check < 0.005:",
      if (max(abs(nb$obs_minus_formula)) < 0.005) "PASS" else "FAIL", "\n")
}
```

The formula values come from ADEMP §7.2 item 3 (`nsim_<tissue>_crule.log`). Because c does not depend on depth, the same values apply to the HD pilots.

# 5. Values passed to the protocol

## 5.1 n_sim

```{r nsim}
#| results: asis
show_pilot("nsim")
```

The `nsim` tables above take the maximum over all pilot conditions of the c-rule pilots, 4,900 UMI included. The design value uses the HD level only (DECISIONS 2026-11-12, precised 2026-11-16): the colon pilot rerun with φ from 50,000 cells (rows at 175 UMI per cell of `rmse_pairs`) and the HD pilots of lymph node and brain with RCTD `UMI_min_sigma` = 100 (`<tissue>_crule_hd_s100_pilot_rmse_pairs.csv`, one depth level each).

```{r nsim-hd}
nsim_hd <- do.call(rbind, lapply(tissues, function(t) {
  if (t == "colon") {
    x <- rd_pilot(t, "rmse_pairs")
    if (!is.null(x)) x <- x[x$depth == 175, ]
  } else {
    x <- rd_pilot(t, "rmse_pairs", variant = "crule_hd_s100")
  }
  if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0) return(NULL)
  r <- x[which.max(x$sd_diff_upper), ]
  data.frame(tissue = t, depth = if (is.null(r$depth)) NA else r$depth, sd_upper = r$sd_diff_upper, arm = r$dataset,
             n_cells = r$n_cells, pair = r$pair, n_sim = ceiling((4 * r$sd_diff_upper / 0.02)^2))
}))
kable(nsim_hd, digits = 4)
```

Expected from DECISIONS 2026-11-12: colon 0.0543 (n_sim 118), lymph node 0.0402 (65), brain 0.0425 (73; 0.0407 before RCTD `UMI_min_sigma` = 100), so n_sim = 118 in every tissue. The largest SD comes from spatialDWLS − NNLS in arm C− at 10 cells in the colon.

## 5.2 Runtimes and cost

Mean seconds per dataset of 500 spots at 175 UMI per cell (`mean_seconds` in `<tissue>_crule_pilot_summary.csv`).

```{r cost}
#| results: asis
for (t in tissues) {
  x <- rd_pilot(t, "summary")
  cat("\n\n**", t, "**\n\n", sep = "")
  if (is.null(x)) { cat("*not available yet*\n"); next }
  x <- x[x$depth == 175, ]
  print(kable(aggregate(mean_seconds ~ method + n_cells, x, mean), digits = 0))
}
```

The same at the HD level of the main run (colon rows at 175 UMI per cell, lymph node and brain HD pilots with `UMI_min_sigma` = 100), which the cost check with n_sim = 118 uses.

```{r cost-hd}
#| results: asis
for (t in tissues) {
  x <- rd_hd(t, "summary")
  cat("\n\n**", t, "**\n\n", sep = "")
  if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) == 0) { cat("*not available yet*\n"); next }
  print(kable(aggregate(mean_seconds ~ method + n_cells, x, mean), digits = 0))
}
```

Cost check with the c-rule pilots (server, 2026-11-11, `scripts/06c_pilot_cost.R`; ADEMP §6): CPU-hours per replicate colon 1.18, lymph node 2.54, brain 11.0, with MuSiC taking 68% of the CPU time. A brain worker peaks at 14–16 GB, so the brain runs with at most 5 workers. With two depth levels and 169 replicates the brain needed 15.5 days against a 12-day window; with one level, 7.7 days. With n_sim = 118 at the HD levels (server, 2026-11-17; colon pilot rerun at 175 UMI per cell, HD pilots of lymph node and brain at 62 and 121 with RCTD `UMI_min_sigma` = 100), CPU-hours per replicate are colon 0.68, lymph node 0.97 and brain 5.18, so the brain needs 5.1 days with 5 workers (colon 0.3, lymph node 0.3) against the 12-day window. MuSiC still takes 67% of the CPU time. Computing the MuSiC basis once per tissue adds margin. The identity check against `music_prop()` passed (24 of 24 datasets identical, MuSiC time 60% of the original; DECISIONS 2026-11-12, precised 2026-11-17). cell2location timing and n_c2l: [TO FILL] (DECISIONS 2026-11-04, dated amendment before the run).

# Closure

**Verdict.** Closed with reservations. The "done" criterion of week 2 is met, because the ADEMP was approved by Luca on 2026-11-18 (PROTOCOLLO §6; DECISIONS 2026-11-18), and the md5 check on lesexp (C2) passed on 2026-11-16. Two reservations remain. The cell2location seed check (C9) and its timing, from which n_c2l is computed, need the GPU and will be written as a dated amendment before the main run (DECISIONS 2026-11-04). At the HD levels the smallest C− − E gap is below δ in the lymph node at 2 cells (§4.1), a result carried to T5.

**Adversarial review.** Run on 2026-11-20 on lesexp in a separate session, independent of the sessions that wrote the pipeline code. It used its own script (`~/scratch/t2_review.R`, outside the repository) that recomputes the key numbers from the pilot CSV files without calling the pipeline functions, and compares them with the values written in this report (56 items, `t2_review_summary.csv`). (1) n_sim. The largest upper SD of the paired differences is 0.05431 in the colon, 0.04018 in the lymph node and 0.04245 in the brain, giving n_sim 118, 65 and 73, so the design value is 118, as in §5.1. (2) Null baseline. The Dirichlet concentrations c and the formula values match §4.2, and the observed null RMSE differs from the formula by at most 0.0006 in every tissue and cells level, HD pilots included. (3) Depth. No spot is below the target in the colon at 175 UMI per cell or in the HD pilots of lymph node and brain. (4) C− against E. 24 of 24 with smallest gap 0.0226 at 175 UMI per cell, as in §4.1. (5) Residues. The minima and counts of negative values match C10 and the tolerance rule gives 1e-4. Six items of (5) are marked as mismatches only because the report writes "PASS both" and the script writes "PASS@1e-5, PASS@1e-4". The meaning is the same, so they are not discrepancies. One real discrepancy was found. At the HD levels of the main run the smallest C− − E gap is 0.0047, below δ, which the earlier verdict of §4.1 did not cover. It is now reported in §4.1 as a result and carried to T5.
